title: Adaptive POP selection using fused p50/p95 latency telemetry and network integrity gating
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Build an adaptive POP (point-of-presence) selector that fuses short- and long-tail latency signals (p50 and p95) together with lightweight network integrity indicators (packet-loss estimates, TCP retransmit hints, and infra heartbeat gaps) to make robust routing decisions and trigger tiered fallback to lower-cost or more robust model variants. This ticket covers design, implementation plan, rollout strategy, monitoring, and the initial canary rollout.

Motivation: Current region selection relies primarily on coarse rolling averages of latency which underweights tail spikes and transient packet-loss events. This leads to two classes of issues: 1) user-visible tail latency regressions when p95 deteriorates but p50 remains stable; 2) noisy region flaps when short-duration anomalies cause aggressive traffic shifts. We need an algorithm that (a) detects long-tail degradation, (b) avoids overreacting to transient noise, and (c) gracefully fails over to compatible model variants (e.g., smaller quantized or lower-context variants) when network integrity is compromised.

Design overview:
- Inputs: per-POP telemetry streams: per-request latency histograms (sampled, aggregated), p50/p95 windows, EWMA of p95 (decay tau configurable), packet-loss proxy (synth from infra ACK stats), TCP retransmit indicator, and health heartbeats.
- Scoring: compute two normalized scores: latency_score = weighted_norm(p50, p95) where p95 is given higher weight (default ratio 2:1) so tails matter; integrity_score = composite(packet_loss, retransmit_rate, heartbeat_misses) normalized 0..1. Final_pop_score = latency_score * (1 - integrity_penalty(integrity_score)). integrity_penalty is a squashed function (sigmoid) to escalate penalties once integrity crosses a threshold.
- Hysteresis & smoothing: apply a two-tier temporal guard: short-term buffer (30s EWMA) and medium-term confirmation window (5 min median) before moving >25% traffic to another POP. This reduces flapping while allowing timely reaction to real outages.
- Tier routing & fallback variants: each POP entry has prioritized model variants (primary full-precision, fallback quantized, fallback small-context). When integrity_score > 0.2 or p95 EWMA exceeds SLO threshold for 2 consecutive confirmation windows, route new traffic to the next variant in the POP's priority list for that customer tier. Variant compatibility table maintained in config.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressiveness vs stability: we prefer conservative movements (avoid churn) because model warm caches and KV caches have cold-start cost. We biased toward slower median confirmation, then accelerated if integrity signals are severe.
- Centralized vs decentralized scoring: single central scorer simplifies policy changes and observability but introduces coupling; we adopted a hybrid: local POP pre-filter for extreme integrity failures (fast path), central scorer for nuanced rank decisions.
- Weighting p50 vs p95: domain teams asked for p95 dominance to preserve UX. We left weighting configurable per-customer tier.

Implementation notes:
- Telemetry pipeline: reuse the existing telemetry ingestion (metrics-collector -> timeseries store), add a lightweight rollup job that emits p50/p95 per-pop per-customer-tier with two windows (30s, 5m) and an EWMA stream for p95.
- Scorer service: new stateless service implemented in Go, reads fused streams from Kafka and writes decisions to routing-consul/edge-config store. Decisions include pop_ranking and variant_recommendation with TTLs.
- Safety: every decision includes a fallback policy and reason code. On decision path failure, route to global fallback POP per-region.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for scoring function including edge cases (zero requests, noisy spikes).
- Synthetic injection tests: fuzz packet-loss and latency spikes in staging to validate hysteresis and variant escalation thresholds.
- Canary: start with internal-only customers in us-west-2 with 5% of traffic for 48h; observe p95 user impact, failed requests, and cost delta.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Dashboards: pop_score_timeseries, p50/p95 EWMAs, integrity_score distributions, decision_count_by_reason, variant_escalation_events.
- Alerts: auto-alert on >3 POPs where integrity_score > 0.25 for >2m, and on routing flaps >3 shifts in 10m.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy telemetry rollups (stage) — 1 week
2) Deploy scorer service in staging and run shadow decisions — 3 days
3) Canary (internal) 5% traffic 48h — evaluate
4) Expand to small set of real customers (opt-in) 2 weeks
5) Global default for non-sensitive customers after 6 weeks depending on metrics

Docs & links:
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/PR-1234 (design v1)
- Implementation PR (initial): https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-routing/pull/219
- Telemetry rollup PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/482
- Dashboard queries: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/PopScores/region-selection

Open questions / next steps:
- Determine per-customer tier weighting matrix for p50/p95 (PM to provide recommended defaults).
- Add cost-awareness: consider model-unit cost delta when escalating variants to avoid large cost regressions.
- Evaluate ML-based anomaly detector to flag early network integrity issues.

Acceptance criteria:
- Shadow mode decisions must match manual evaluation for >95% of cases over a 72-hour run in staging.
- Canary must not increase 99th-percentile end-to-end latency for canary customers by more than 5%.
- Observability dashboards and alerting in place before traffic moves.
